subject: SKU allocation & risk-bucket plan for NovumAI Dedicated commitment
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-07-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: SKU allocation & risk-bucket plan for NovumAI Dedicated commitment

Team —

NovumAI execs asked us to give a concrete SKU split for their 12-month Dedicated commitment. They want predictable latency for chat features but also run a small set of long-context batch transforms that are memory-heavy. I sketched a risk-bucket approach and attached a draft workbook (novum-risk-buckets.xlsx) and a high-level SKU proposal (sku-proposal.pdf).

Key constraints from the commercial thread:
- Start window: Oct 1 target
- Min guaranteed concurrency: 200 concurrent sessions (chat) with p50 latency SLA 150ms
- Occasional long-context batch jobs (~6% of token volume) that need >=100GB model memory or aggressive tiling
- Budget sensitivity: willing to prioritize latency for 70% of traffic, accept cheaper fallback for background jobs

Proposal (high-level):
- Risk buckets: latency-sensitive (70%), throughput/scale (24%), memory-bound batch (6%)
- SKU map: H100 for memory-bound / long-context, A100 for latency-sensitive mix, L4 for high-throughput cheap inference and overflow
- Pilot: reserve a small pilot pool (10 H100-equivalent slots) to validate long-context perf and kernel behavior before full commit

Ask: please review the workbook and flag any ops or perf risks. Dev — can you validate the H100->A100 fallback path for KV cache and tiling? Irene — ops, what lead time do we need to provision the pilot H100 seats and a contiguous L4 pool for burst? Lauren — I need a recommended commercial split (percentages and optional discounting triggers) to share with NovumAI by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Deals, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

On 2028-07-18 09:12, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> Team —
>
> (summary omitted)

Thanks for the clear framing. Quick tech notes from my side after a fast pass through the workbook:

1) Memory-bound bucket (H100):
- H100 gives us headroom for large KV caches and tiling; it handles 100GB+ model footprints with fewer tiling penalties.
- For the Novum long-context models (checkpoint sizes ~70–110GB) H100 with 80-bit workspace works best; we avoid multi-node KV shards where possible.
- Risk: quantization/INT8 paths on H100 are still in evaluation; if they want aggressive quant we need to validate model accuracy.

2) Latency-sensitive (A100):
- A100 is the sweet spot for p50/p95 latency on 16–32k context chat use-cases given current kernels.
- With continuous batching (small batch sizes) we can preserve p50 while pushing throughput.
- Risk: if their traffic has spiky large-context requests, p95 will climb; recommend dynamic routing based on predicted seq-length.

3) Throughput / low-cost scale (L4):
- L4 is great for productionizing high QPS cheap responses (short prompts, high concurrency).
- Downside: limited memory for long contexts; must be used for short-context fallthrough and cached responses.

4) Fallback & routing:
- Plan an automated routing policy: prefer A100 for live chat, route to L4 when tokens/<prompt < 1024 and predicted latency budget allows, and route to H100 for explicit long-context jobs tagged in the request.
- KV cache portability: ensure cache keys map across variants or accept cache miss penalty when falling back from H100->A100/L4.

5) Pilot sizing:
- Pilot H100: 10 slots (equiv to 10 H100 GPUs) should cover validation; run a 2-week synthetic and 1-week customer beta.
- L4 pool: 50–100 slots depending on expected QPS; we can right-size after 48h of telemetry.

I can run a short benchmark matrix next week if we lock down the model checkpoint and sequence-length distribution.

- Dev
Lead Systems Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-07-18T13:35:00Z
Subject: Re: SKU allocation & risk-bucket plan for NovumAI Dedicated commitment

Karthik / team —

Thanks, this is helpful. Commercial constraints / asks from my side after speaking to Novum finance:
- Novum can commit to a 12-month reserved spend but needs price certainty for the year. They prefer fewer SKU types for accounting simplicity (ideally 2 SKUs).
- They will accept a third SKU as a burst / fallback (L4) but want a clear pricing delta and usage thresholds that trigger burst billing.
- They want a default split proposal we can negotiate: looking for a simple 70/20/10 tiered split but with the ability to reclassify up to 5% between tiers after the pilot.

Suggested commercial mapping to match Ops/Dev guidance:
- Primary: A100 (70%) — covers latency-sensitive chat and avoids overpaying for H100 for most traffic
- Secondary: L4 (20%) — default inexpensive layer for short-context scale and cached hits
- Memory reserve: H100 (10%) — for long-context models and scheduled batch windows

Discounting triggers:
- If Novum pushes >10% of tokens into memory-bound during normal hours, offer a 5% rebate for the months exceeding the threshold (protecting us from unexpected memory demand).
- Pilot credit: absorb first 2 weeks of pilot H100 infra costs; thereafter bill pro-rated.

I can draft the split and insertion language into the term sheet. Dev/Irene — confirm provisioning lead time and whether we can enforce usage classification via routing rules (so accounting aligns with billing).

-Lauren
Sr. Deal Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Torres <elena@novum.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: SKU allocation & risk-bucket plan for NovumAI Dedicated commitment

Karthik / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the workbook and internal telemetry (link to usage): https://app.novum.ai/org/usage/overview

- Current profile: ~78% short chat prompts (avg len 220 tokens), 16% medium multi-turn (1k–3k tokens), 6% nightly batch long-context jobs (often >32k tokens). Peak QPS seen in PST business hours.
- We are fine with a 2-SKU core if that makes things simpler; we mainly want predictable p95 for the chat experience.
- Long-context jobs are non-critical to user-facing latency but have strict accuracy requirements; they can be scheduled to run in a reserved window if that makes provisioning easier.

We appreciate the pilot offer and would like to start the pilot in early September if that's doable. We'll share a sample usage CSV (attached) for Dev to benchmark.

Best,
Elena Torres
VP, Platform Engineering
NovumAI

Subject: Re: SKU allocation & risk-bucket plan for NovumAI Dedicated commitment

Thanks all — summary and actions below. Quoting Dev and Lauren inline where helpful.

Decision summary (agreed tentative):
- Commercial split to propose to Novum: A100 70% / L4 20% / H100 10% (pilot-adjustable +/-5%) — matches Novum's preference for 2 main SKUs with an explicit memory reserve.
- Pilot: 10 H100-equivalent slots for early-Sept start, 50 L4 slots for burst/scale validation. Dev will run benchmarks on the sample usage CSV.
- Routing & billing: Ops to enforce classification rules; L4 usage billed at burst rates when routing falls back automatically. Lauren to encode thresholds and rebate triggers in term sheet.

Open ops items:
- Irene: provisioning lead time for pilot H100 seats and whether we can guarantee contiguous tenancy for the reserved window.
- Dev: timeline for benchmark (aiming for 7 business days after receiving model checkpoints).

Next steps:
- Lauren to send draft commercial split language to Novum by EOD Friday.
- Dev & Irene to confirm pilot provisioning timeline by Wednesday.
- Karthik to own deal note and coordinate procurement (ticket DED-1245).

Thanks — will push the term sheet once we have provisioning confirmation.

Karthik
Head of Deals, Dedicated
Redwood Inference
